OpenLara is credited as a reference for TR1 data formats, while this repository describes the Jaguar engine as original work.

projects.summary: A Rust/C++ rebuild of the Gamebryo/Creation Engine lineage that reads Bethesda NIF, BSA/BA2, ESM/ESP and script data through a new engine and Vulkan renderer. The README lists seven Bethesda game targets, says the project does not redistribute their game data, and frames the result as a reference implementation. It is a multi-title engine reimplementation, not a recompilation of the original executables.
projects.strategy: Maintainer-described ground-up Rust/C++ engine reimplementation using reverse-engineered and documented game data formats; it does not execute or statically recompile the original game binaries. The clean-room description is the project's own claim, not an independent legal finding.
projects.source_available: Public source repository on GitHub. GitHub reports no detected project license, the repository root has no LICENSE file, and the only license file found in the recursive repository tree is for the vendored FidelityFX SDK. Public visibility does not establish reuse rights for ByroRedux code; the README’s FOSS-only statement is maintainer intent, not a published license. The project says it does not bundle Bethesda game data, which users must supply.
